Benchmark.title: AEGIS Network Infrastructure Security Benchmark
Benchmark.description: Network infrastructure security assessment based on NIST SP 800-41, CIS Controls, and PTES standards. Evaluates firewall rules, exposed services, port security, and network segmentation.

Rule.title: Unnecessary Services Must Not Be Exposed
Rule.description: Only ports required for the application's function should be externally accessible. All other ports must be filtered by firewall rules. Unnecessary exposed services expand the attack surface and provide additional entry points for attackers.
Rule.fixtext: Review all open ports and close unnecessary services. Configure host firewall (iptables/nftables) and network firewall to only allow required traffic.

Rule.title: SSH Must Be Hardened per CIS Benchmark
Rule.description: SSH service must disable root login, password authentication (use key-based), and protocol version 1. MaxAuthTries should be 4 or fewer. AllowUsers/AllowGroups should restrict access. Port should be non-default if possible.
Rule.fixtext: Set: PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no, Protocol 2, MaxAuthTries 4, AllowUsers authorized_user

Rule.title: Database Ports Must Not Be Externally Accessible
Rule.description: Database services (MySQL 3306, PostgreSQL 5432, MongoDB 27017, MSSQL 1433, Redis 6379) must not be accessible from untrusted networks. Direct database exposure enables brute force, SQL injection, and unauthorized data access.
Rule.fixtext: Bind database to 127.0.0.1 or internal network only. Block database ports at the firewall. Use SSH tunnels or VPN for remote database administration.

Rule.title: Remote Desktop Services Must Require VPN Access
Rule.description: VNC (5900) and RDP (3389) must not be directly exposed to the internet. These protocols have a history of critical vulnerabilities (BlueKeep CVE-2019-0708) and are prime targets for brute force attacks.
Rule.fixtext: Block VNC/RDP at the perimeter firewall. Require VPN connection before remote desktop access. Enable Network Level Authentication for RDP.

Rule.title: SMB/NetBIOS Must Not Be Internet-Facing
Rule.description: SMB (445) and NetBIOS (135, 139) ports must never be exposed externally. EternalBlue (MS17-010), WannaCry, and NotPetya all exploited exposed SMB services. These protocols are designed for internal LAN use only.
Rule.fixtext: Block ports 135, 139, 445 at the perimeter firewall. Disable SMBv1. Ensure Windows Firewall blocks these ports for public profiles.

Rule.title: DNS Recursion Must Be Disabled for Public-Facing DNS
Rule.description: Public-facing DNS servers must not allow recursive queries from external sources. Open recursive DNS servers can be abused for DNS amplification DDoS attacks and cache poisoning.
Rule.fixtext: Set 'allow-recursion { localhost; internal-network; };' in BIND config. For other DNS servers, restrict recursion to trusted clients only.

Rule.title: FTP Must Be Replaced with SFTP/SCP
Rule.description: Plain FTP transmits credentials and data in cleartext. FTP servers are frequently vulnerable to bounce attacks and directory traversal. SFTP or SCP should be used for all file transfer needs.
Rule.fixtext: Disable FTP service. Replace with SFTP (SSH subsystem) or SCP. If FTP is required, enforce FTPS (FTP over TLS) with certificate validation.

Rule.title: Telnet Must Be Disabled
Rule.description: Telnet transmits all data including passwords in cleartext and has no encryption. It must be replaced by SSH for all remote administration. Telnet is considered deprecated and insecure by all modern security standards.
Rule.fixtext: Disable telnet service: systemctl disable telnet.socket. Remove telnet server package. Use SSH exclusively for remote administration.

Rule.title: ICMP Rate Limiting Should Be Configured
Rule.description: ICMP responses should be rate-limited to prevent information disclosure and ICMP-based attacks. However, ICMP should not be completely blocked as it's essential for path MTU discovery and network diagnostics.
Rule.fixtext: Configure iptables rate limiting: iptables -A INPUT -p icmp --icmp-type echo-request -m limit --limit 1/s -j ACCEPT

Rule.title: Network Segmentation Must Be Implemented
Rule.description: Production, development, management, and DMZ networks must be logically or physically segmented. Flat networks allow lateral movement after initial compromise, enabling attackers to pivot to critical assets.
Rule.fixtext: Implement VLANs for network segmentation. Configure inter-VLAN routing with ACLs. Place web servers in DMZ. Restrict management network access.
